extracted.intended_audience: AI/ML researchers and practitioners evaluating large language models' mathematical reasoning
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating a large language model's mathematical problem-solving ability, including correctness of approach, calculation accuracy, generalization, and modeling skills, across benchmarks and hand-crafted examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to identify which arguments, intermediate steps, calculations or algebraic manipulations are likely to be relevant at each stage, in order to chart a path towards the solution. This component is often based on a heuristic guess (or in the case of humans, intuition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the model picks an appropriate high-level strategy (e.g., writing recurrence relations, arguing about polynomial degrees, choosing case splits). Consider whether the model proposes heuristics before performing detailed calculations. Examples: model correctly chooses to write recurrence relations in the population problem; chooses degree argument for polynomial composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical proficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to perform routine calculations or manipulations that follow a prescribed set of steps (such as differentiating a function or isolating a term in an equation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether algebraic manipulations, arithmetic, and routine steps are carried out correctly. Note: the paper finds frequent mistakes in arithmetic, order of operations, and notation; suggests that access to code execution could reduce such errors. Use manual inspection to separate reasoning from calculation mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to critically examine each step of the argument, break it down into its sub-components, explain what it entails, how it is related to the rest of the argument and why it is correct; includes backtracking when steps are realized to be incorrect and modifying the argument accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the model can detect and correct its own mistakes, provide justification for steps, and perform an 'inner dialogue' of verification. The paper notes a significant deficiency here and attributes it to training data lacking explicit inner-dialogue and to next-token prediction not enabling revision of previous outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct problem formulation / reformulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to restate or reformulate a problem in an equivalent, helpful way (e.g., expressing the population question as f(f(f(x))) = 27x − 26).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score positively when the model produces a sound reformulation that clarifies structure or enables a correct solution path. Example: GPT-4 correctly reformulates the population-change problem using function composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appropriate proof techniques (e.g., induction) and quantifier handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct selection and application of proof techniques such as induction, and proper handling of quantifiers in generalizations (ensuring that 'for some constants' vs 'for any constants' is treated correctly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that induction base and step are valid and that quantifier scope matches the problem statement. The paper highlights GPT-4's incorrect handling of quantifiers in a generalization attempt and its invalid induction argument as failure modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree/structure reasoning for polynomials and function composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizing structural constraints such as degrees of polynomial compositions and using them to deduce impossibility (e.g., degree-2 polynomial composed three times gives degree 8, incompatible with a degree-1 target).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the model reasons about algebraic structure (degree, closure under composition) before attempting brute-force calculation; reward concise structural arguments that avoid heavy computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class closure under composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying whether a class of functions is closed under composition (e.g., linear functions remain linear under composition), and correctly characterizing which classes have that property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate claims about closure (the paper flags GPT-4's incorrect claim that exponential and logarithmic classes are closed under composition). Expect correct definitions and examples; flag conceptual confusions about definitions (e.g., varying definitions of 'exponential function').

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish approach correctness from arithmetic/calculation errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Separating whether the model used the correct high-level approach from whether it made arithmetic or algebraic mistakes in execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating model outputs, score approach and calculations separately. The paper's manual inspection finds GPT-4 often uses the correct approach but fails due to arithmetic errors; evaluation should capture that distinction (e.g., correctness of method vs final numeric accuracy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark single-model accuracy on math datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Measured per-question correctness (single-model accuracy) on standard math benchmarks such as GSM8K, MATH, and MMMLU-STEM (reported: GPT-4 87.1% on GSM8K, 42.5% on MATH, 82.7% on MMMLU-STEM in the paper's experiments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report these accuracy numbers and compare models. Use these as coarse-grained performance metrics but combine with qualitative analysis of error types to understand failure modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error taxonomy and distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorization of wrong solutions by type: arithmetic mistakes (including counting), misunderstanding the problem statement, and wrong approaches. (Paper reports: 68% arithmetic mistakes, 10% misunderstanding, 22% wrong approaches among sampled wrong answers.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When auditing failures, classify errors according to this taxonomy and report percentages from manual inspection. Use this to prioritize fixes (e.g., if majority are arithmetic, add computation tools).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating memorization / overfitting checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies to reduce the likelihood that high benchmark performance is due to memorization of dataset instances rather than general reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper's strategies: (1) ask model to write a template solution (no numbers), (2) ask for steps-first then final answer, (3) vary numbers in representative problems and check consistency, (4) craft new questions unlikely to appear online. Use these tests to detect memorization and evaluate robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Template generation capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to generate a symbolic/template solution (a solution template without concrete numbers) for word problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the model can produce a reusable template mapping problem structure to symbolic solution steps. Example template for tomatoes problem provided in paper; reward clear symbolic formulations and stepwise templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorization test by alternating numeric values
rubrics_metrics.description: Testing whether the model memorized exact problem statements by altering numerical values and checking if the model still applies a general solution method (paper reports GPT-4 75.2% on altered GSM8K example while text-davinci-003 had 0.2%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use randomized numeric perturbations of benchmark problems and measure stability of answers; robust generalization implies similar accuracy under perturbation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual-inspection sampling methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Manually inspect a random selection of model wrong answers (e.g., 100 wrong answers) to identify common error modes and quantify their frequencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible, perform manual audits on a representative sample to obtain fine-grained diagnostics (the paper used this to produce Table 4). Document sampling method and inter-annotator agreement if multiple raters are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance on Fermi questions / order-of-magnitude reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to answer Fermi-style estimation tasks by layering reasonable assumptions and informed guesses, using order-of-magnitude reasoning and plausible intermediate estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the model produces a clear chain of assumptions, justifies approximations, and yields an interpretable final estimate with uncertainty bounds. Reward models that show layered reasoning even when final numeric is rough.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical modeling of real-world scenarios
rubrics_metrics.description: Capacity to build plausible mathematical models for interdisciplinary real-world problems (e.g., profiling physiological power rate over time of a pro StarCraft 2 player), including variable definitions, assumptions, and example parameter estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the model defines variables clearly (P(t), B, A, f(t), g(r)), states assumptions and simplifications, proposes parameter estimation methods, and provides example instantiation. Evaluate concision and plausibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher-level mathematics / creative proof ability
rubrics_metrics.description: Capability to solve or produce correct proofs for non-template problems requiring creative argumentation (e.g., simplified IMO-style problems).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate correctness and originality of proofs, whether the model chooses appropriate case splits or constructive definitions, and whether the reasoning is logically coherent. Use such examples to probe the model's creative reasoning limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness to phrasing/context changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensitivity of model reasoning to wording variations — whether slight changes in question phrasing alter the model's displayed knowledge or solution capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test multiple equivalent formulations of the same problem; if performance varies widely, flag context-dependence. The paper notes GPT-4's mathematical knowledge is context-dependent and that wording changes can alter displayed knowledge.
